summary: Snapshot 2026-10-27. Nothing today meets the strict Lane C test (a randomized efficacy result first made public within 48 h). The UBT251 Cell Metabolism paper came out Oct 26, but its topline numbers were announced earlier, so it goes to a Short. The best long-form opportunities are Lane A topics that this week's news has refreshed. (1) Nutrient gaps on GLP-1 medicines: The Independent ran it Oct 26, Harvard Health and Science Focus have covered it, and several cohorts link these medicines to vitamin D, iron and B-vitamin gaps. This is the fresh hook for "Protein on Tirzepatide". (2) Bones and muscle: the Arch Osteoporos systematic review (Oct 23) and 10 snapshots of steady momentum. (3) Stopping (SURMOUNT-4 plus the Oct 19 persistence paper). (4) Hair loss, with the Oct 9 systematic review of skin side effects. Shorts: UBT251 versus semaglutide 1 mg (Phase 2, published Oct 26; frame it as 'Novo's answer to retatrutide'), retatrutide sleep apnea 'what's confirmed' (peaking, but Gizmodo and Medscape picked it up again Oct 26), ACOG pregnancy guidance (CBS, Oct 26), Halloween food noise (peaks Oct 31), and the Lilly Q3 call (Oct 29), held for a Lane C slot only if a new headline number comes out. Microdosing and retatrutide sourcing stay rejected.

candidates.topic: Protein, vitamin D, iron and B12 gaps on tirzepatide: what the new nutrient-deficiency research shows (Independent Oct 26; Harvard Health; claims cohort of ~500,000 GLP-1 users)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why'. Open on a 'you' scenario: you're eating half as much, so what's missing? Answer in 15 s: protein and a few nutrients are the usual gaps. The research is observational ('linked to'). Give practical protein-first habits and suggest asking your prescriber about checking levels. No supplement doses.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream UK pickup (The Independent, Oct 26) of deficiency research that is still spreading through Harvard Health, Science Focus and Yahoo. It fits the playbook's planned Lane A 'Protein on Tirzepatide' slot exactly, and big channels haven't packaged it as a tirzepatide question yet.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 regain, plus new real-world persistence and discontinuation data (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A: open with 'you're thinking of taking a break'. Give the answer up front: in SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36), people switched to placebo regained much of the weight. Then real-world numbers on how often people stop, and why that matters. Say plainly: 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own; talk to your prescriber'. Fix L1's dropped-numbers issues.

candidates.topic: UBT251, Novo's triple-G agonist, versus semaglutide 1 mg in type 2 diabetes: randomized Phase 2 now published in Cell Metabolism (Oct 26)
candidates.angle: Short at 13:00: 'Novo's answer to retatrutide?' 211 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, 24 weeks. Weight down up to 9.8% versus 4.8% on semaglutide 1 mg and 1.4% on placebo; HbA1c down up to 2.16 points versus 1.77 and 0.66. Investigational, Phase 2, a small trial in one country. Loop ending.

candidates.angle: Lane A: 'you're seeing more hair in the brush'. Answer: hair shedding was reported by a minority in the trials and is usually linked to rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium). It's often temporary. Protein and steady nutrition help, and see your clinician if it persists.
